title: Chapter 5 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of S3 and EBS – from buckets and encryption to volume types and snapshots.

questions.question: S3 is an example of which type of storage?
questions.explanation: S3 is object storage – it stores data as objects in buckets, accessible via HTTP API.

questions.question: Which statement about S3 bucket names is true?
options: They must be unique within a region
They must be globally unique across all AWS accounts
They can be renamed after creation
questions.explanation: Bucket names are globally unique. You cannot rename a bucket; you must delete and create a new one.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of a single object in S3?
questions.explanation: A single S3 object can be up to 5 TB in size. Larger files must be uploaded via multipart upload.

questions.question: Which S3 feature adds a delete marker to an object instead of permanently removing it?
questions.explanation: With versioning enabled, a simple delete adds a delete marker. To permanently delete, you must specify a version ID.

questions.question: You want to automatically move objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard‑IA after 30 days and to Glacier after 90 days. What should you use?
questions.explanation: S3 Lifecycle configuration defines transition and expiration actions based on age or date.

questions.question: Which encryption option gives you full control over the encryption keys and integrates with AWS CloudTrail for auditing?
questions.explanation: SSE‑KMS uses AWS KMS, which provides separate permissions, key rotation, and CloudTrail logging.

questions.question: What does the 'Block Public Access' setting in S3 do?
options: Prevents any public access, overriding bucket policies and ACLs
Sends alerts when a bucket becomes public
questions.explanation: Block Public Access provides a centralised control to prevent public exposure, even if a bucket policy would otherwise allow it.

questions.question: When both an IAM policy and a bucket policy apply, what is the evaluation logic?
options: The IAM policy overrides the bucket policy
The bucket policy overrides the IAM policy
Access is granted if either policy allows and neither denies
questions.explanation: S3 evaluates the union of IAM and bucket policies; an explicit Deny in either denies access.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class is designed for data that is accessed less frequently but requires millisecond retrieval?
questions.explanation: Standard‑IA provides low latency and high throughput for infrequent access. Glacier has retrieval delays.

questions.question: EBS volumes can be attached to multiple EC2 instances simultaneously.
questions.explanation: False. An EBS volume can only be attached to one instance at a time (except for multi‑attach on io2, which is a special case).

questions.question: An EBS volume in us-east-1a can be attached to an EC2 instance in:
questions.explanation: EBS volumes are locked to a single AZ. The instance must be in the same AZ.

questions.question: Which EBS volume type is not bootable?
questions.explanation: st1 and sc1 are HDD‑based and cannot be used as boot volumes. Only SSD types can be boot volumes.

questions.question: What is the baseline IOPS for a 200 GB gp3 volume?
questions.explanation: gp3 provides a baseline of 3,000 IOPS for any size; you can provision extra for an additional cost.

questions.question: A 100 GB gp2 volume provides what baseline IOPS?
questions.explanation: gp2 gives 3 IOPS per GB, so 100 × 3 = 300 IOPS, with the ability to burst up to 3,000 for short periods.

questions.question: EBS snapshots are stored in:
questions.explanation: Snapshots are backed by S3, though they are not visible in the S3 console. They are incremental.

questions.question: How can you move an EBS volume to a different Availability Zone?
options: Detach and reattach in the new AZ
Create a snapshot and restore it in the new AZ
questions.explanation: Snapshots are region‑wide. You can create a volume from a snapshot in any AZ within the same region.

questions.question: Which AWS service can automate EBS snapshot scheduling?
questions.explanation: DLM automates the creation, retention, and deletion of EBS snapshots according to policies.

questions.question: You need the lowest cost archive for data accessed once a year, with 12‑hour retrieval time. Choose:
questions.explanation: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest storage class, designed for long‑term retention with retrieval times of 12–48 hours.

questions.question: Which of the following is required for Cross‑Region Replication?
options: Both buckets must have Block Public Access enabled
Versioning must be enabled on both source and destination buckets
The buckets must be in the same account
The source bucket must use SSE‑KMS
questions.explanation: Versioning is mandatory for CRR. The buckets can be in different accounts.

questions.question: You have an unencrypted EBS volume that needs to be encrypted. What is the process?
options: Enable encryption on the volume directly
Snapshot the volume, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, then create a new volume from the encrypted snapshot
Attach the volume to an encrypted instance
questions.explanation: EBS encryption cannot be added to an existing volume in‑place. You must go through the snapshot copy process.
